registered: 2026-10-07 07:30, round 2, before any probe of this round was run; the L = 96 counterflow control (W2) is integrating and unread
scoring: prepare.py unchanged: score = min(D,5)/5 * novelty * reach/3 / (1 + cost_days/5); 'realistic' is the cost term (days of compute + analysis on this machine with the present code)
sources: D1-D7 of docs/designs/RESEARCH_DIRECTIONS_2026-10-07.md and the five external directions pasted by the owner on 2026-10-07 (R1-R5); overlaps merged: R1 = D1 + the acoustic-memory reading; R2 = D7; R3 = D2

hypotheses.short: Self-generated counterflow: a single shrinking pair in a closed box stalls at b(d0, L, T) while zero-impulse pairs do not (D1 / R1a)
hypotheses.statement: The impulse shed by a shrinking pair drives a normal-fluid drift u = 2 pi rho_s (d0 - d)/(rho_n L^2) that reduces the friction drive; stall when pi rho_s d0^2 > 2 rho_n L^2, no stall in a larger box; the drift is visible as an occupation anisotropy n_k - n_-k.
hypotheses.rival: The stall is intrinsic to the pair (box-independent), or an artefact of the run.
hypotheses.probe: Existing data: late/early d^2-slope ratio of the two single pairs against the zero-impulse pairs at the same T, and the phonon-band momentum slope; D = contrast of late slopes between single and zero-impulse pairs in jackknife sigma.
hypotheses.lean_companion: wind_stall extended to the torus drive; counterflow momentum balance as an identity

hypotheses.short: Acoustic memory: the vortex velocity autocorrelation has a negative lobe at the box acoustic time L/c, and diffusion is Markovian only beyond it (R1b)
hypotheses.statement: In a closed box the vortex is dressed by its own shed sound returning across the periodic boundaries; the residual-velocity autocorrelation shows negative memory at lags ~ L/c = 64 (and harmonics), and the sub-diffusive exponent 0.71 at short lags is this memory.
hypotheses.rival: Monotone (Markovian) decay of the velocity autocorrelation; the short-lag plateau is detection jitter only.
hypotheses.probe: VACF of the residual velocities (after the two-coefficient fit) of the 16 tracked vortices at T/T_BKT = 0.14; D = depth of the most negative lobe in lags 40-100 in bootstrap sigma; consistent only if that lobe is negative.
hypotheses.lean_companion: generalised fluctuation-dissipation identity for a linear memory kernel (finite-dimensional)

hypotheses.short: The Josephson offset eta_g1 K - 1 = +0.3 is the amplitude (density) fluctuations in g1: the phase-only correlator obeys eta K = 1 (D2 / R3)
hypotheses.statement: g1 = <psi* psi> decays faster than the phase correlator <exp(i(theta - theta'))> because density fluctuations are correlated with phase gradients near vortex cores; the phase-only exponent satisfies eta_phase K = 1 within 0.1 while eta_g1 K - 1 = +0.3.
hypotheses.rival: Both exponents carry the same offset (the offset is in K or in the relation), or the phase-only exponent overshoots.
hypotheses.probe: Equilibrated L = 192 snapshots (30 per run, 6 runs): eta from g1 and from the phase-only correlator on the same windows with the torus Green function; D = |x_g1 - x_phase| / sigma over runs; consistent if x_phase within 0.1 of 0.
hypotheses.lean_companion: Gaussian phase-field correlator identity on the torus (exp of minus half the variance)

hypotheses.short: The friction law alpha = 0.24 rho_n/rho: the prefactor is set by the Rayleigh-Jeans phonon bath up to the cutoff and shifts with cutoff and mg (D7 / R2)
hypotheses.statement: alpha/rho_n is constant in T at fixed cutoff (established to ~15 %) and changes with the cutoff and the core profile in the way classical phonon scattering off a Bernoulli core predicts.
hypotheses.rival: alpha/rho_n is a universal constant independent of cutoff; or alpha is not proportional to rho_n beyond the three measured points.
hypotheses.probe: Existing data: proportionality test alpha = c rho_n/rho across the three temperatures with jackknife errors; D = c / sigma_c (how well the law is determined) and consistency of a zero intercept.
hypotheses.lean_companion: momentum-transfer integral of a plane wave scattering off a 1/r velocity field (Born), as a definite integral identity

hypotheses.short: The box-scale pair's longevity is microcanonical: with a damping (canonical) term the same pair decays much faster (R4)
hypotheses.statement: Unwinding a box-scale pair in an energy-conserving periodic field requires its impulse and energy to be absorbed by the finite phonon bath; a damped GPE at the same temperature removes that bottleneck and the decay time drops by a large factor.
hypotheses.rival: The decay time is set by the pair's own friction and is the same with or without a damping term of comparable strength.
hypotheses.probe: Five-minute simulation: L = 24, a pair of d0 = L/2 - 2 at T = 0.115 (thermal state scaled from e0.60), 120 time units each in the PGPE and in the damped GPE (gamma = 0.02); D = |Delta d| at the end over the detection resolution 0.3.
hypotheses.lean_companion: energy barrier of a dipole crossing the periodic boundary at fixed total energy and momentum (lower bound)

hypotheses.short: Quantum vacuum noise (truncated Wigner) restores a transverse force: alpha' moves from 0 toward rho_n/rho (R5)
hypotheses.statement: Adding half a quantum per mode breaks the classical scattering symmetry so that alpha' becomes positive and grows with the quantum fluctuation parameter.
hypotheses.rival: alpha' stays zero within 1 % with vacuum noise added.
hypotheses.probe: Five-minute simulation: antiparallel pairs at L = 32 in the thermal state with half-quantum noise added to every mode, 80 time units; D = |Delta(1 - alpha')| / sigma against the classical value -- expected unresolvable in the budget.
hypotheses.lean_companion: Wigner-Weyl symmetric-ordering map of the point-vortex observables (not attempted)

hypotheses.short: Vortex versus phonon share of the stiffness near BKT: the vortex polarisability with the tight-pair current form factor accounts for less than half of rho_n(k1) in equilibrium (D3)
hypotheses.statement: In the equilibrated L = 192 states most of the transverse response is phononic; the vortex share, (1 - f)^2 mu(d)^2 Sigma d^2 /(2 T L^2) with mu the T = 0 form factor, is below 0.5 of rho_n(k1).
hypotheses.rival: The vortex share is the majority (Kosterlitz-Thouless with point vortices).
hypotheses.probe: Existing primary_C4.json: share = n_eff_raw^2 R_Tv / R_T per run; D = |0.5 - median share| / sigma over the five runs without a box-scale pair.
hypotheses.lean_companion: PairPolarisation response ceiling with a form factor

hypotheses.short: Equilibration-time statistics of the last box-scale pair versus L (z from S_q(k_min, t)) (D5; H06 of round 1)
hypotheses.statement: The drop time of the box-scale charge over seeds and sizes gives z where vortex-density estimators fail; one L = 192 trajectory exceeds 13 500.
hypotheses.probe: Round-1 probe H06 re-run unchanged (ln Q1 vs ln N_v over the depressed runs).
hypotheses.lean_companion: MatchingScreening lower bound on the remaining equilibration time

hypotheses.short: Cutoff law of the classical-field BKT point (D6; H09 of round 1)
hypotheses.statement: n_c lambda^2 = ln(380/g) + ln(E_cut/T), slope 1 in ln E_cut.

hypotheses.short: Einstein relation at a second admitted temperature (D4)
hypotheses.statement: With a cleaner T ~ 0.3 base and 5000-time-unit tracks the residual exponent enters [0.8, 1.2] and R_E lies in [0.5, 2].
hypotheses.rival: R_E > 2 at every admitted temperature (excess diffusion is real).
hypotheses.probe: Existing data: R_E at the one admitted temperature; D = |R_E - 1| / sigma (how far the present data sit from Einstein).
